messages:
mira: hey team, Mira here — first week! kicked off my feature branch CI on Buildkite and the job fails when pushing the image to GHCR with 403. who should i ping for quick perms help? :wave:
sam: welcome Mira! pinging @jordan too. usually that 403 means the GitHub App used by Buildkite doesn't have package write perms or the repo wasn't included in the app install. can you paste the exact error?
ci-bot: Buildkite job #8421 for mira/feat/fast-start failed: step "publish-image" exited with status 1. https://buildkite.example.com/organizations/redwood/pipelines/inference/builds/8421
mira: here's the docker output i see in the job logs:
```
Pushing to ghcr.io/redwood-inference/fast-start:sha-abc123
ERROR: Denied: GET https://ghcr.io/v2/: 403 Forbidden
failed to push some refs to 'ghcr.io/redwood-inference/fast-start'
```
jordan: yep that's classic. two quick things to check: 1) under org settings > GitHub Apps > "redwood-ci-app" ensure it has access to Packages and write permission; 2) the app installation must include this repo or "all repositories"; if it's a private repo and the app wasn't granted access, you'll see 403 on push.
mira: i checked and redwood-ci-app shows installed but only "Selected repositories" and my repo isn't listed. added it just now. should i re-run?
sam: re-run the pipeline after adding. also verify the Buildkite pipeline's credentials are the GitHub App installation token and not an old PAT. we recently rotated PATs so some older pipelines still reference them.
ops-oncall: quick FYI — we don't want people generating PATs for CI unless it's an emergency. if adding the repo doesn't fix it, ping infra-owners and we can rotate the installation token or check the buildkite webhook mapping.
mira: re-run done — same 403. buildkite still using ghcr push step that references `BUILDKITE_GITHUB_APP_TOKEN` env var. where can i check the token mapping?
jordan: go to Buildkite pipeline settings -> Environment -> check pipeline-level env vars. if token is set there it's probably the old PAT. pipeline-level vars are editable by pipeline admins. if it's in credentials store (Vault) we should see a secret name. can you paste the pipeline env list (redact values)?
mira: pasted in private — it shows BUILDKITE_GITHUB_APP_TOKEN set at pipeline-level (looks like a PAT). i don't have perms to change pipeline envs.
sam: OK, two options: 1) infra team can switch that var to a short-lived app installation token (we have a script), or 2) add a deploy key with write:packages to the repo. i'd prefer (1) for org consistency. @ops-oncall can you help swap the pipeline var?
ops-oncall: on it. i will rotate the variable to use the app installation token and re-run. will comment here once done. :gear:
ci-bot: Buildkite job #8422 queued (retry by ops-oncall).
ops-oncall: swapped the pipeline env var to app token and kicked off the build. monitoring logs now.
ci-bot: Buildkite job #8422 for mira/feat/fast-start started.
ci-bot: Buildkite job #8422 step "publish-image" succeeded.
mira: omg thank you!! that fixed it. hugely appreciated — happy to sit with someone for a quick walkthrough so i don't block others. :pray:
sam: awesome — we'll add a short doc in eng-infra onboarding about verifying the pipeline token source. mira, i'll DM you for a walkthrough slot.
jordan: adding checklist item: confirm pipeline tokens are not hard-coded PATs; prefer GitHub App tokens. i'll open a tiny PR to the onboarding repo.
mira: sweet. thanks everyone!
